Subject: Re: Intermittent slow completions — now sustained

Neha,

We're seeing a sustained degradation across our production workloads since ~07:30 PT. Symptoms: p95 ~4.2s (usually ~350ms), p99 ~12s (usually <1s), and a spike in 5xx errors (~3% of requests) coincident with a ~25% drop in throughput. This is directly impacting our checkout pipeline — failures are user-visible.

Attached is a short sample of error logs and a trace around a failed request (harborcloud_error_snap_20280824.log). We haven't changed anything on our side. Please treat this as urgent — we need either an immediate mitigation or a rollback path.

Can you confirm whether there were any deployment changes on your side or if our traffic is being routed differently? We're available on a call now.

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, HarborCloud

Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: sustained long-tail latency & errors impacting HarborCloud

Quick initial findings from the 08:30–09:10 PT window (attached trace: trace-20280824-harborcloud.json):
- We see heavy queue buildup on the model-serving pool assigned to HarborCloud. Prefix cache hit rate dropped ~60% for that tenant during the window.
- Concurrency enforcement: the tenant is at the configured concurrency cap (100 concurrent streams) and requests are piling up, which explains tail amplification and timeouts.
- A handful of workers exhibited elevated GC/eviction events — likely worsening KV cache churn.

Short-term mitigations tested in staging (recommendation):
1) Temporarily increase the tenant concurrency cap to 250 (will reduce queueing head-of-line wait).
2) Enable per-tenant burst capacity for the next 2 hours.
3) Turn on an aggressive prefix cache warming policy for the customer's model (best-effort).
4) If errors persist, route a subset of traffic to a slightly smaller model variant (faster to serve) as fallback.

Caveats: increasing concurrency will raise token cost and may surface other resource contentions if other tenants also burst. Need ops approval and monitoring. I can push a change now if we have a quick green light.

Attaching kvcache heatmap snapshot (kvcache-heatmap-aug24.png) and link to live dashboard: https://redwood.prod.dash/harborcloud/requests?p95=4200&p99=12200

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

Neha / Dylan —

Thanks for the rapid triage. From a CS perspective, HarborCloud is in a high-impact checkout path and we should prioritize mitigation over cost for the next 120 minutes. Proposed runbook for immediate execute:
- Approve increasing concurrency to 250 for HarborCloud for 2 hours (Dylan to push).
- Enable burst capacity and monitor error rate and p99 every 2 mins.
- Open a targeted circuit-breaker at the route layer to reject known malformed high-cost requests.
- Notify HarborCloud that we're implementing these steps and share rollback criteria.

I'll own communication to the customer and the bridge. Neha, want me to take lead on the call notes?

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir@harborcloud.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Aug 2028 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: sustained long-tail latency & errors impacting HarborCloud

FYI — We implemented the temporary mitigations at 10:12 PT yesterday as follows:
- Concurrency cap for HarborCloud bumped from 100 -> 250 (applied to model pool ID: mp-hc-42).
- Burst capacity enabled (2h window).
- Cache warming policy toggled and a lightweight cache prefill for top prefixes.

Results in first 40 minutes post-mitigation: p95 dropped to ~420ms, p99 to ~980ms, errors down to 0.4%, throughput back to ~95% of baseline. Monitoring is steady.

Next steps (longer-term):
- Root-cause follow-up: KV cache churn appears related to recent kernel-level allocator changes we rolled in the last runtime deploy. Recommend a rollback of that allocator change for the impacted pool and a controlled canary for the fix.
- Work with Optimize team to create per-tenant cache-sizing recommendations and adaptive concurrency autoscaler.
- Postmort (RT-4312) to include timeline, mitigation, and engineering action items.

I'll schedule a readout with Eng + CS + Sales for Monday EOD to assign owners. Great work triaging quickly.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Runtime Engineering, Redwood Inference
